title: Pericoli per la salute: i verbi modali e i consigli

sentences.it: Dovresti indossare la mascherina quando l'aria è inquinata.
sentences.en: You should wear a mask when the air is polluted.
alternatives: You should wear a mask when the air's polluted.
sentences.hint: should per un consiglio — wear, mask, polluted

sentences.it: Non dovresti mangiare tanti hamburger: sono malsani.
sentences.en: You shouldn't eat so many hamburgers: they're unhealthy.
alternatives: You shouldn't eat so many hamburgers: they are unhealthy.
You should not eat so many hamburgers: they're unhealthy.
You should not eat so many hamburgers: they are unhealthy.
sentences.hint: shouldn't per un consiglio — so many, hamburgers, unhealthy

sentences.it: In Inghilterra devi guidare sul lato sinistro della strada.
sentences.en: In England you must drive on the left side of the road.
alternatives: You must drive on the left side of the road in England.
In England you must drive on the left-hand side of the road.
sentences.hint: must per un obbligo — drive, left side, road

sentences.it: Le fabbriche non devono gettare rifiuti nel fiume.
sentences.en: Factories mustn't throw waste into the river.
alternatives: Factories must not throw waste into the river.
Factories mustn't throw waste in the river.
Factories must not throw waste in the river.
sentences.hint: mustn't per un divieto — factories, throw waste, river

sentences.it: Stasera potrebbe piovere.
sentences.en: It might rain tonight.
alternatives: It may rain tonight.
It could rain tonight.
It might rain this evening.
It may rain this evening.
It could rain this evening.
sentences.hint: might per una possibilità — rain, tonight

sentences.it: Potrei andare in palestra più tardi.
sentences.en: I might go to the gym later.
alternatives: I may go to the gym later.
I could go to the gym later.
sentences.hint: might per una possibilità — gym, later

sentences.it: Posso aprire la finestra?
sentences.en: May I open the window?
alternatives: Can I open the window?
Could I open the window?
sentences.hint: may per chiedere il permesso — open, window

sentences.it: Mio fratello sa nuotare molto bene.
sentences.en: My brother can swim very well.
sentences.hint: can per un'abilità — swim, very well

sentences.it: Sono molto stressata per il lavoro: cosa dovrei fare?
sentences.en: I'm very stressed about work: what should I do?
alternatives: I am very stressed about work: what should I do?
I'm very stressed about my work: what should I do?
I am very stressed about my work: what should I do?
sentences.hint: stressed about + should nella domanda — work

sentences.it: Potresti metterti a dieta.
sentences.en: You could go on a diet.
sentences.hint: could per un suggerimento — go on a diet

sentences.it: Perché non vai dal medico?
sentences.en: Why don't you go to the doctor?
alternatives: Why don't you go to the doctor's?
Why don't you see a doctor?
sentences.hint: suggerimento con why don't you — go to the doctor

sentences.it: Che ne dici di fare più esercizio?
sentences.en: How about doing more exercise?
alternatives: What about doing more exercise?
sentences.hint: suggerimento con how about + -ing — do, more exercise

sentences.it: Che ne dici di andare a correre domani mattina?
sentences.en: How about going running tomorrow morning?
alternatives: What about going running tomorrow morning?
How about going for a jog tomorrow morning?
What about going for a jog tomorrow morning?
sentences.hint: suggerimento con how about + -ing — go running, tomorrow morning

sentences.it: Non bere alcolici se prendi le medicine.
sentences.en: Don't drink alcohol if you take medicine.
alternatives: Do not drink alcohol if you take medicine.
Don't drink alcohol if you're taking medicine.
Don't drink alcohol if you are taking medicine.
Do not drink alcohol if you are taking medicine.
sentences.hint: imperativo negativo con don't — drink alcohol, take medicine

sentences.it: Dovresti fare delle pause mentre lavori.
sentences.en: You should take breaks while you're working.
alternatives: You should take breaks while you are working.
You should take breaks while you work.
sentences.hint: should + while con il present continuous — take breaks

sentences.it: Pensi che il tuo quartiere sia inquinato? Sì, credo di sì.
sentences.en: Do you think your neighbourhood is polluted? Yes, I think so.
alternatives: Do you think your neighborhood is polluted? Yes, I think so.
sentences.hint: do you think + risposta breve I think so — neighbourhood, polluted

sentences.it: Pensi che i fertilizzanti siano nocivi? Non credo.
sentences.en: Do you think fertilizers are harmful? I don't think so.
alternatives: Do you think fertilisers are harmful? I don't think so.
Do you think fertilizers are harmful? I do not think so.
Do you think fertilisers are harmful? I do not think so.
sentences.hint: do you think + risposta breve I don't think so — fertilizers, harmful

sentences.it: Pensi che passerai l'esame? Spero di sì.
sentences.en: Do you think you'll pass the exam? I hope so.
alternatives: Do you think you will pass the exam? I hope so.
sentences.hint: do you think + will, risposta breve I hope so — pass the exam

sentences.it: Pensi che domani la spiaggia sarà affollata? Spero di no.
sentences.en: Do you think the beach will be crowded tomorrow? I hope not.
alternatives: Do you think the beach is going to be crowded tomorrow? I hope not.
sentences.hint: do you think + will, risposta breve I hope not — beach, crowded

sentences.it: Mio padre è molto in forma perché fa esercizio ogni giorno.
sentences.en: My father is very fit because he does exercise every day.
alternatives: My father is very fit because he exercises every day.
My dad is very fit because he does exercise every day.
My dad is very fit because he exercises every day.
sentences.hint: present simple — fit, because, do exercise, every day

Farmers shouldn't use too many pesticides.
Smoking is harmful to your lungs.
vocabulary.mnemonic: harm è il danno: harmful, pieno di danno, nocivo.

This fertilizer helps plants grow.
My sister is vegetarian, so she doesn't eat meat.

You shouldn't listen to loud music with earphones.

vocabulary.example: The factory near the river pollutes the water.

vocabulary.example: Cars pollute the air.

My dad went on a diet after the holidays.
She wants to lose weight before the summer.
I always gain weight at Christmas.

This river is very polluted.
I feel stressed before exams.
The bus is always crowded in the morning.

vocabulary.example: My grandmother is very fit for her age.

vocabulary.example: Fresh fruit is good for your health.
Too much sugar is bad for your health.
I try to eat healthy food.
Fast food is very unhealthy.
I go to the gym after work.
I swim every Tuesday.
Let's go running in the park.

I have an English exam on Friday.
I need to revise for my exam.

vocabulary.example: My classmate helped me with my homework.
The city should ban cars from the centre.

vocabulary.example: Climate change is a big problem for everyone.
My neighbourhood is quiet and safe.
vocabulary.mnemonic: neighbour è il vicino: neighbourhood è il vicinato, il quartiere.

grammar.title: I verbi modali
grammar.body:
I verbi modali sono verbi ausiliari: dopo di loro viene il **bare infinitive**, cioè l'infinito senza *to*.

- *Factories must respect laws about waste.* — Le fabbriche devono rispettare le leggi sui rifiuti.

A differenza dell'ausiliare *do*, i modali **non prendono la -s** alla terza persona: tutte le persone hanno la stessa forma.

**soggetto + verbo modale + bare infinitive**

- *You should go home.* / *She should go home.* — Tu dovresti / Lei dovrebbe andare a casa.

## A che cosa servono

| Verbo modale | Negativa | Uso |
| --- | --- | --- |
| *could* | *could not* / *couldn't* | abilità, possibilità, consiglio, permesso informale |
| *may* | *may not* | permesso formale, possibilità |
| *might* | *might not* | possibilità |
| *should* | *should not* / *shouldn't* | consiglio |
| *must* | *must not* / *mustn't* | obblighi, raccomandazioni |

Altri modali di uso comune:

- *shall* — per suggerire qualcosa, solo con *I* e *we*: *Shall I open the window?* — Apro la finestra?
- *will* — per formare il futuro semplice: *I will drive to work.* — Andrò al lavoro in auto.
- *can* — per la capacità di fare qualcosa: *I can cook.* — So cucinare.

## Possibilità: could, may, might

Quando descrivono la possibilità di fare qualcosa, *could*, *may* e *might* sono intercambiabili.

- *You could go right or left to get to my house.* — Potresti andare a destra o a sinistra per arrivare a casa mia.
- *We may go to the centre by car or by tram.* — Potremmo andare in centro in macchina o in tram.
- *I might call you later.* — Potrei chiamarti più tardi.

## Consiglio e obbligo: should, must

*Should* / *shouldn't* danno un consiglio; *must* descrive un obbligo.

- *You should wear a mask in the city.* — Dovresti indossare una mascherina in città.
- *You shouldn't drink too much alcohol!* — Non dovresti bere tanto alcol!
- *You must drive on the right side of the road in Italy.* — Devi guidare sul lato destro della strada in Italia.

grammar.title: Dare consigli
grammar.body:
Per dare un consiglio a qualcuno ci sono due gruppi di espressioni.

## Con il bare infinitive

*should*, *shouldn't*, *could*, *don't*, *why don't you* + infinito senza *to*:

- *You should stop smoking.* — Dovresti smettere di fumare.
- *You shouldn't drink alcohol.* — Non dovresti bere alcol.
- *You could go to the gym.* — Potresti andare in palestra.
- *Don't smoke.* — Non fumare.
- *Why don't you go swimming?* — Perché non vai a nuotare?

## Con il gerundio

*How about* / *What about* + verbo in **-ing**:

- *How about seeing a doctor?* — Che ne dici di andare dal medico?
- *What about eating healthy food?* — Che ne dici di mangiare del cibo sano?

## Esempio di dialogo

- *I'm very stressed about my exams. What should I do?* — Sono molto stressato per gli esami. Cosa devo fare?
- *You should take breaks while you are studying.* — Dovresti fare delle pause durante lo studio.
- *Why don't you revise with your classmates?* — Perché non ripassi con i tuoi compagni di classe?
- *How about going for a jog?* — Che ne dici di andare a correre?

grammar.title: Rispondere con so: I think so, I hope so
grammar.body:
Per rispondere a una domanda senza ripeterla tutta si usa *so*.

## I think so / I don't think so

*I think so* dice che credi che una cosa sia vera; secondo il tono può indicare un po' di incertezza. Al negativo si dice *I don't think so*.

- *Do you think London's parks are polluted?* — *Yes, I think so.* (Sì, credo di sì.)
- *Do you think smoking should be banned completely?* — *I don't think so.* (Non credo.)

## I hope so / I hope not

Con *hope* al posto di *think* dici che **vorresti** che una cosa succedesse, o che non succedesse.

- *Do you think we can reverse climate change?* — *I hope so.* (Spero di sì.)
- *Do you think that drugs will ever be legalised?* — *I hope not.* (Spero di no.)

## Attenzione

Le due negative si costruiscono in modo diverso: *I **don't** think so*, ma *I hope **not*** (mai *I don't hope so*).
